items.text: In the 16-bed intensive care unit, will a lean redesign of the morning sedation interruption process raise completed interruptions from 38 to 70 percent of eligible patient-days between November 2026 and April 2027, without an increase in self-extubation?
items.population: Eligible ventilated patient-days on continuous sedation
items.intervention: Countermeasures from value stream mapping and A3 cycles (approval step removed for patients passing the screen, shared 08:00 time with respiratory therapy)
items.comparator: Eight-week baseline of the current process
items.outcome: Weekly proportion of eligible patient-days with a completed interruption
items.time: Eight baseline weeks, then November 2026 to April 2027
items.setting: 16-bed medical and surgical intensive care unit

finer: Feasible within the facilitator's hours and existing charting; interesting to nurses, therapists and physicians; novel only locally; ethical as service improvement with safety monitoring; relevant because trial benefits depend on adherence.
summary: One time-bound improvement aim with a safety limit.
